notes: Flight-cage experiment shows feeding anthers preferentially manipulated and pollinating anthers disproportionately export pollen to other flowers.
Natural pollen differences and manipulations show feeding anthers attract bees while pollinating-anther pollen is much more likely to reach stigmas.
Feeding-anther removal lowers visitation and pollen receipt; heteranthery and pollen allocation are experimentally characterized.
Predominantly selfing congener retains heteranthery but shows disproportionate reduction in feeding-anther pollen allocation; direct pollinator manipulation was focused on M. korsakowii.
Study reports dimorphic stamen/pollen traits and higher pollen viability in long pollinating stamens; not a complete direct pollen-fate experiment.
